section_1.title: The Hook: The Bouncing Blocks Puzzle
section_1.content: Introduce the physical setup: Two blocks of different masses on a frictionless surface. Block A (mass m) slides toward Block B (mass M=100^n * m) which is initially stationary. Both bounce off the wall and each other. We count the total number of collisions until they move away forever.
section_1.example: Visualize a small hamster-sized block (m) hitting a giant elephant-sized block (M) that is against a wall.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: Conservation of Momentum and Energy
section_2.content: Briefly review elastic collisions. In a 1D elastic collision, both kinetic energy and momentum are conserved. We represent this on a 2D phase-space plot: momentum vs. position, which reveals a circular arc trajectory.
section_2.example: Display a graph where the x and y axes represent the velocities of the blocks. The collision path traces an arc of a circle.

section_3.title: The Geometric Bridge: Mapping Collisions to Angles
section_3.content: Explain that every collision corresponds to an angular rotation on a circle. The ratio of the masses determines the angle of the arc. As the mass ratio M/m increases, the number of collisions grows to reflect the digits of Pi.
section_3.example: An animation showing a light ray reflecting inside a circular mirror (billiard ball model) to demonstrate how the geometry maps to the block collisions.

section_4.title: The Connection: Why Pi?
section_4.content: Explain the convergence: When M/m = 100^n, the number of collisions is exactly the first n+1 digits of Pi. This highlights the deep, unexpected link between discrete physical interactions and transcendental constants.
section_4.example: A table showing m=1, M=100 resulting in 31 collisions (first two digits of Pi: 3.1).

section_5.title: Summary and Implications
section_5.content: Conclude by emphasizing that computational physics often uses physical analogies to solve complex mathematical problems. Encouraging students to see the 'geometry' hidden in 'motion'.
section_5.example: Final screen showing a 3D animation of the blocks merging into the symbol 'π'.
